title: ICH E2A — Clinical Safety Data Management
summary: Defines standards and terminology for expedited ICSR reporting during clinical development. Establishes core definitions of 'serious', 'unexpected', and 'adverse drug reaction'. Primary reference for SUSAR reporting timelines (7-day/15-day) and causality assessment criteria.

title: ICH E2B(R3) — Electronic Transmission of ICSRs
summary: Defines the HL7/XML data element structure and format for electronic ICSR submissions to regulatory authorities. E2B(R3) is the current mandatory format for EudraVigilance (EU), PMDA (Japan), and increasingly FDA.

title: ICH E2C(R2) — Periodic Benefit-Risk Evaluation Report (PBRER)
summary: Establishes the harmonized format for periodic safety reporting for approved marketed products — the PBRER/PSUR. Defines International Birth Date (IBD), Data Lock Point (DLP), and submission timelines.

title: ICH E2D — Post-Approval Safety Data Management
summary: Defines adverse event reporting obligations for marketed products including expedited 15-day and periodic reporting. Provides the regulatory basis for post-marketing ICSR definitions, spontaneous reporting, literature monitoring, and solicited reports.

title: ICH E2E — Pharmacovigilance Planning
summary: Framework for proactive pharmacovigilance at the time of regulatory approval including risk management planning and signal detection planning. Forms the regulatory basis for the EU RMP and FDA REMS.

title: ICH E2F — Development Safety Update Report (DSUR)
summary: Defines the format and content of the annual safety report for investigational medicinal products during clinical development. Replaces FDA IND Annual Report safety sections and aligns with EU CTA annual requirements.

title: ICH E6(R2/R3) — Good Clinical Practice (GCP)
summary: Governs sponsor obligations for AE/SAE reporting, investigator safety reporting, DSMBs, and trial master file requirements. E2B-compliant SAE data structures apply under GCP.

title: ICH E8(R1) — General Considerations for Clinical Studies
summary: Updated guideline integrating quality-by-design principles into trial design; includes risk-proportionate approaches to safety data collection and monitoring that affect PV obligations during development.

title: 21 CFR Part 312 — IND Safety Reporting
summary: Governs IND safety reporting obligations. Section 312.32 requires 7-day fatal/life-threatening SUSAR reports and 15-day reports for serious unexpected ADRs. Section 312.33 requires annual progress reports (DSUR equivalent). Section 312.32(c)(1)(ii) governs co-sponsor SUSAR obligations.
source_label: 21 CFR 312 (eCFR) · FDA IND Safety Reporting Guidance (2015)

title: 21 CFR Part 314 — NDA Post-Marketing Safety Reporting
summary: Section 314.81 governs post-marketing safety reporting for NDA holders: 15-day alert reports, PADERs (Periodic Adverse Drug Experience Reports), and Field Alert Reports (314.81(b)(1)).

title: 21 CFR Part 601 — BLA Post-Marketing Safety Reporting
summary: Governs post-marketing safety reporting for biologics. Section 600.80 covers adverse experience reporting including 15-day expedited reports and periodic reporting. Section 600.81 covers distribution reporting.

title: 21 CFR 314.81(b)(1) — Field Alert Reports (FARs)
summary: Requires NDA holders to submit Field Alert Reports within 3 days for product quality, safety, or labeling issues: contamination, chemical/physical change, product mix-up, or labeling issues. Critical for CMO oversight.

title: REMS (21 CFR 505-1 / FDAAA §505-1) — Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategies
summary: Mandates risk minimization programs for high-risk drugs including Medication Guides, Communication Plans, and Elements to Assure Safe Use (ETASU). MAHs must implement, monitor, and assess REMS effectiveness.

title: 21 CFR Part 4 — Combination Products
summary: Governs classification and regulatory pathway for drug-device-biologic combinations. PV obligations follow the primary mode of action; both drug and device reporting frameworks may apply simultaneously.

title: 21 CFR Part 11 — Electronic Records and Electronic Signatures
summary: Governs use of electronic records and e-signatures in FDA-regulated activities. Directly applicable to PV safety databases, audit trail requirements, and validated system controls. Critical for BIMO inspection readiness.

title: 21 CFR Part 211 — cGMP for Finished Pharmaceuticals
summary: Intersects PV through product quality complaints, OOS investigations, and manufacturing deviations that generate or substantiate safety signals. CMO-reported issues may trigger PV obligations.

title: FDAAA 2007 / Sentinel Initiative — Postmarketing Safety Provisions
summary: Establishes FDA authority to require post-marketing studies, mandate REMS, and require label changes. Established the Sentinel Initiative for active drug safety surveillance using large US healthcare databases.

title: MedWatch / FAERS — FDA Safety Reporting & Adverse Event Database
summary: MedWatch (Form 3500A) is the mandatory ICSR reporting system. All data flows into FAERS — the national PV database used for signal detection (disproportionality analysis). Public access via openFDA API.
source_label: MedWatch Portal · FAERS Database · openFDA API

title: VAERS — Vaccine Adverse Event Reporting System
summary: Joint FDA/CDC passive surveillance system for vaccine adverse events. Mandatory reporting for healthcare providers and vaccine manufacturers. Data used by CDC ACIP and FDA VRBPAC for benefit-risk assessments.

title: BIMO — Bioresearch Monitoring Program
summary: FDA's inspectional authority covering clinical investigators, IRBs, sponsors, and CROs. Audits ICSR quality, SUSAR reporting timeliness, IND annual report accuracy, and safety data reconciliation.

title: FDA RWE Framework (2018/2023) — Real World Evidence for Post-Market Safety
summary: Guidance on using real world data and RWE for post-marketing safety decisions, label updates, and PMC/PMR fulfillment. Sentinel System study protocols are the primary RWD application for post-marketing safety.

title: Regulation (EU) No 1235/2010 + Directive 2010/84/EU — EU PV Legislation
summary: Overarching EU PV legislative framework. Establishes EMA's PRAC, defines MAH obligations, mandates the QPPV role, requires the PSMF, and establishes the GVP framework. All EU MAHs must comply.

title: Regulation (EU) 726/2004 — Centralized Procedure and EMA Powers
summary: Governs the centralized marketing authorization procedure and EMA's post-marketing powers including urgency procedures, referrals, and suspension of MA. PRAC recommendations carry direct PV enforcement authority.

title: GVP Module I — Pharmacovigilance Systems and Quality Systems
summary: Defines MAH requirements for PV quality system: quality management, SOPs, training, audits, PSMF, and QPPV oversight. Mandates minimum SDEA content.

title: GVP Module II — Pharmacovigilance System Master File (PSMF)
summary: Detailed requirements for the PSMF including mandatory content, update frequency, inspection access, and QPPV certification. The PSMF is an inspectable document.

title: GVP Module III — Pharmacovigilance Inspections
summary: Framework for NCA and EMA inspections of MAH PV systems. Covers pre-inspection, on-site, and post-inspection phases; critical findings definitions; and CAPA requirements.

title: GVP Module IV — Pharmacovigilance Audits
summary: Requirements for routine and triggered PV system audits by MAHs. Minimum every 2 years; auditor independence; audit report content; outputs feed into PSMF.

title: GVP Module V — Risk Management Systems
summary: Defines the structure and content of the EU Risk Management Plan (RMP). Covers safety specification, pharmacovigilance plan, risk minimization, and additional risk minimization measures (aRMM). Required at MA and updated at each renewal/variation.

title: GVP Module VI — Collection, Management and Submission of ADRs
summary: Governs ICSR collection, processing, and submission timelines to EudraVigilance. Defines seriousness, expectedness, causality, and electronic transmission in E2B(R3). Core operational PV module.

title: GVP Module VII — Periodic Safety Update Reports
summary: Defines PSUR/PBRER format, content, and submission timelines for EU MA holders. Covers PSUR work-sharing procedure. PRAC assesses PBRERs and may issue recommendations impacting MA.

title: GVP Module VIII / VIII(a) — Post-Authorisation Safety & Efficacy Studies
summary: Module VIII governs design, conduct, and reporting of non-interventional PASS. Module VIII(a) covers PAES required as MA conditions. PASS protocol must be submitted to EMA/PRAC via ENCEPP.

title: GVP Module IX — Signal Management
summary: Defines the EU signal management process: detection in EVDAS, validation, prioritization, assessment, and PRAC review. MAHs must monitor PRAC signals quarterly.

title: GVP Modules X–XVI — Additional Monitoring through Risk Minimisation Effectiveness
summary: Module X: Additional Monitoring (▼ symbol). Module XI: Public participation. Module XII: Continuous benefit-risk. Module XIII: Incident management. Module XIV: International collaboration. Module XV: Safety communications (DHPC). Module XVI: Risk minimization effectiveness evaluation.

title: GVP Product/Population Addenda — Vaccines (Add. I), Biologicals (Add. II), Paediatrics (Add. III)
summary: Addendum I covers vaccine PV specifics. Addendum II covers biologicals/biosimilars immunogenicity. Addendum III covers paediatric PV obligations under PUMA.

title: EudraVigilance / EVDAS — EU Central ICSR Database
summary: EMA's central database for ADR reports. MAHs submit ICSRs in E2B(R3) format. EVDAS is used by EMA/PRAC and MAHs for signal detection. Direct access available to MAHs.

title: EU CTR / Regulation 536/2014 — Clinical Trial Regulation
summary: Electronic SUSAR reporting through the CTIS portal. Sponsors submit SUSARs within 7/15 days. Annual DSUR required for ongoing EU trials. Supersedes Directive 2001/20/EC.

title: Japan — PMDA/MHLW (Ministerial Ordinance 171 / GPSP / GVSP) — Japan PV Framework
summary: Japan's core PV framework: Ministerial Ordinance 171 governs ICSR collection and reporting to PMDA; GPSP governs post-marketing clinical studies; GVSP governs MAH PV system requirements. Re-examination periods (4–10 years) require active data collection.

title: Canada — Health Canada (Food and Drug Regulations Part C, Div. 8) — Canada PV Framework
summary: Requires MAHs to submit serious ADR reports within 15 days and non-serious ADRs within 90 days. Summary safety and efficacy reports (PSUR equivalent) submitted at defined intervals. Canada Vigilance program collects all reports.
source_label: Canada Vigilance Program · Health Canada PV Guidance

title: Australia — TGA (Therapeutic Goods Act 1989) — Australia PV Framework
summary: Mandatory 15-day reporting for serious unexpected events. PSUR submission required at MA renewal and on request. RMP required for new chemical entities and high-risk products. DAEN is the national ADR database.

title: China — NMPA (China GVP 2021) — China PV Framework
summary: Comprehensive PV framework effective 2021. Requires PV department, designated PV officer, SOP library. ADR reporting within 15 days (serious)/30 days (non-serious). PSUR at 5-year MA renewal intervals.

title: India — CDSCO (Schedule Y + New Drugs & Clinical Trials Rules 2019) — India PV Framework
summary: Schedule Y governs PV reporting. PvPI is the national PV network. PSUR submissions every 6 months for the first 2 years, then annually. Serious unexpected ADRs require 15-day expedited reporting.

title: Brazil — ANVISA (RDC 204/2017) — Brazil PV Framework
summary: Mandates PV system documentation, written procedures, and designated PV officer. Serious AE reports submitted to NOTIVISA within 15 days. RPPS is the PSUR equivalent.

title: South Korea — MFDS (GVP Notice + Pharmaceutical Affairs Act) — South Korea PV Framework
summary: ICSRs submitted to KAERS. PSUR submissions aligned with ICH E2C(R2). Re-examination period (4–6 years) requires active PV data collection.

title: GCC Harmonized PV Guidelines (SFDA-led) — Gulf Cooperation Council PV Framework
summary: Harmonized framework across Saudi Arabia, UAE, Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain, and Oman. ICSR submission to national ADR databases. PSUR timelines aligned regionally. Local PV contact required in each member state.

title: ASEAN Harmonized Technical Requirements — ASEAN PV Framework
summary: Harmonized PV requirements across 10 ASEAN markets. PSUR submission, ICSR reporting, and RMP requirements vary by member state but reference ICH standards. Singapore HSA and Thailand FDA are most ICH-aligned.

title: CIOMS I — International Reporting of Adverse Drug Reactions (1990)
summary: Established the CIOMS I form and a standard set of data elements for reporting individual suspected adverse drug reaction cases internationally. The basis for later ICH ICSR standards (E2B, E2D).

title: CIOMS II–VII — PSUR / CCDS / Benefit-Risk / Clinical Trial Safety / DSUR
summary: CIOMS II: Prototype PSUR format (precursor to ICH E2C). CIOMS III: CCSI/CCDS framework (reference safety information). CIOMS IV: Benefit-risk methodology. CIOMS VI: Clinical trial safety management. CIOMS VII: DSUR framework (precursor to ICH E2F).

title: CIOMS VIII — Signal Detection Methodologies (2010)
summary: Defines quantitative signal detection methods: PRR (Proportional Reporting Ratio), ROR (Reporting Odds Ratio), BCPNN (Bayesian Confidence Propagation Neural Network), and MGPS. Referenced in FDA signal detection guidance and EMA EVDAS methodology.

title: WHO-UMC Causality Assessment + VigiBase — WHO Global PV Framework
summary: WHO-UMC causality scale (Certain/Probable/Possible/Unlikely) used by national PV centers globally. VigiBase is WHO's global ICSR repository with 140+ contributing countries. Used for international signal detection and trend analysis.

title: PIC/S GVP Guidelines — Pharmaceutical Inspection Co-operation Scheme
summary: PIC/S adopts harmonized GVP standards used in Switzerland (Swissmedic), Singapore (HSA), Israel, New Zealand, and other PIC/S member states. PV inspections in these countries reference PIC/S guidance.

title: Radiopharmaceuticals — 21 CFR Part 361 / EMA Guideline — Radiopharmaceutical PV
summary: US: 21 CFR 361.1 governs specific IND/NDA requirements; NRC overlaps on radiation safety. Standard NDA/BLA post-marketing PV obligations apply to approved diagnostic radiopharmaceuticals. EU: EMA guideline covers specific safety reporting, dosimetry data in PV assessments.
source_label: 21 CFR 361 (eCFR) · EMA Radiopharmaceuticals · NRC Drug Oversight

title: Biologics/Biosimilars — 21 CFR 600–601 + EMA Regulation 726/2004 — Biologics PV
summary: Enhanced PV obligations including immunogenicity monitoring, batch surveillance, and comparability data post-approval. Biosimilars require extrapolation of safety data and post-marketing immunogenicity studies.

title: Medical Devices — 21 CFR Part 803 + EU MDR 2017/745 — Device Vigilance
summary: FDA MDR under 21 CFR 803 requires reporting of deaths and serious injuries within 30 days (5 days for certain events). EU MDR 2017/745 requires serious incident reports to national competent authorities.

title: ATMPs — EU Regulation 1394/2007 — Advanced Therapy Medicinal Products PV
summary: ATMPs have 30-year record retention obligations, specific patient traceability requirements, and tailored PASS mandates. PRAC applies increased post-authorization oversight. FDA gene therapy IND/BLA requirements apply in the US.
source_label: EU ATMP Regulation (EUR-Lex) · EMA ATMPs · FDA Gene Therapy Guidance

title: Vaccines — GVP Add. I + 21 CFR Part 600 + VAERS — Vaccine PV
summary: Enhanced passive surveillance via VAERS (US) and EudraVigilance vaccine-specific reporting; active surveillance via VSD (Vaccine Safety Datalink). Benefit-risk assessed in public health context. Batch release PV data required.

title: FDA AI/ML Guidance (2023) — AI/ML in PV Workflows
summary: FDA guidance on AI tools in drug development and post-marketing contexts including AI-assisted ICSR processing, signal detection, and NLP of literature. Relevant for validated PV tools using AI/ML components.
source_label: FDA AI/ML Action Plan · FDA AI Framework

title: EMA AI Strategy / EU Digital Health Act — EU Digital PV
summary: EMA's evolving obligations for AI-assisted signal detection, digital biomarker data in PV submissions, and integration of EHR data into pharmacoepidemiology studies. EU Digital Health Act creates new data governance frameworks affecting PV data flows.
source_label: EMA Digital Strategy · EU Digital Health Act

title: 21 CFR Part 11 + EMA Annex 11 — Electronic System Validation for PV
summary: FDA Part 11 and EMA Annex 11 govern computerized system validation for PV software (safety databases, signal tools, MedDRA coding tools). Audit trails, access controls, and data integrity requirements are inspectable in BIMO and EU PV inspections.

title: Safety Data Exchange Agreements (SDEAs) — Contractual PV Obligations
summary: ICH E2D, GVP Module I, and 21 CFR 312.32(c)(1)(ii) mandate the existence and minimum content of SDEAs between co-MAHs, development partners, CROs, CMOs, and licensees. EMA Q&A on SDEAs (2011) defines binding minimum content. SDEAs are audited during PV inspections.

title: MedDRA — Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities
summary: MSSO-maintained controlled medical terminology required for all ICSR submissions globally. Version controlled — new releases biannually. MAHs must use the current version per regulatory requirements.

title: WHODrug — WHO Drug Dictionary
summary: WHO-UMC maintained drug dictionary for medicinal product coding in ICSRs globally. WHODrug Global format is the standard for EudraVigilance submissions.
